providers.name: Spotify Web API
notes: All endpoints share the host https://api.spotify.com and require an OAuth 2.0 access token in an Authorization: Bearer header.
Catalog endpoints (albums, artists, tracks, search) accept an app-only Client Credentials token. Endpoints under /v1/me require a user token with the listed scopes.

February 2026 Development Mode changes: owner must have Spotify Premium; new apps limited to 5 users; many bulk/browse/user endpoints removed; several response fields removed (album label/popularity/available_markets, track popularity/available_markets/linked_from, artist followers/popularity, several user profile fields); playlist 'tracks' renamed 'items' and playlist contents restricted to playlists the user owns or collaborates on; search limit max reduced to 10.

Removed endpoints (for example Get Artist's Top Tracks, Get New Releases, Get Several Albums, GET /v1/users/{id}/playlists, GET /v1/playlists/{id}/tracks) are intentionally excluded from this library.
Response samples model a Development Mode app: removed fields are omitted from samples but listed in responseFields as deprecated with a note.
Image URLs for playlist images are temporary and expire in less than a day.
Developer policy: Spotify content may not be downloaded, cover art must be shown in original form with a link back to Spotify, and content may not be used to train ML/AI models.

May 2026: account_id was added to the User object returned by Get Current User's Profile; Spotify recommends account_id (stable, pseudonymous) instead of id for linking accounts.
July 2026: a developer may create up to 25 Client IDs (was 1); Development Mode quotas are counted per developer account rather than per Client ID, so several Development Mode apps share one quota.

February 2026 library consolidation: the type-specific save/remove/contains/follow endpoints were replaced by PUT /v1/me/library, DELETE /v1/me/library and GET /v1/me/library/contains, which take Spotify URIs (max 40). The GET list endpoints for saved tracks (/v1/me/tracks), saved albums (/v1/me/albums) and followed artists (/v1/me/following) remain.
Playlists are created with POST /v1/me/playlists (POST /v1/users/{user_id}/playlists was removed) and items are added with POST /v1/playlists/{playlist_id}/items (the /tracks variant was removed).
Apps in Extended Quota Mode are not affected by the February 2026 Development Mode changes (migration guide); this library models a Development Mode app.

explanation.summary: Creating a playlist and filling it are separate requests. The create request returns the new playlist's id, which goes into the add request's path. The songs come from the recently-played response as items[].track.uri, because the add endpoint wants URIs, not IDs. Setting public=false keeps the playlist private, and the create response also provides external_urls.spotify for the link.
keyIdeas: A write request often returns the new resource (201 Created). Read the id from that response; you cannot know it in advance.
Check what format an endpoint expects: Add Items to Playlist takes URIs (spotify:track:...), while most paths take IDs.
Check defaults on write endpoints: public defaults to true, which would break the privacy requirement.
In play history, each entry wraps the song: the URI is items[].track.uri, while played_at belongs to the entry.
Write scopes are separate from read scopes: playlist-modify-private for a private playlist.

scenarios.learningTarget: Chain a write workflow: create a resource, take its returned id into the next request's path, and pass values from another response in the format the endpoint requires (URIs).

instructionalReview.learn: Students learn a create-then-use write flow. They also learn to check the expected identifier format (URI vs ID) and defaults that change behavior (public=true).
